title: Coherence-Based Identification of Carbon-Based Spin Qubits in Hexagonal Boron Nitride from First Principles
authors: Hyeonsu Kim, Jaewook Lee, Huijin Park, Hosung Seo
abstract: Carbon-related defects in hexagonal boron nitride are promising room-temperature single-spin qubits and quantum sensors, but their atomic structures remain largely unidentified. Here we show, using first-principles calculations of electron-spin decoherence, that the atomic structure of each defect is imprinted in its spin coherence. Mapping the Hahn-echo dynamics of seven candidate carbon defects across magnetic field and four isotope-engineered nuclear-spin baths, we find that electron-spin-echo envelope modulation emerges at defect-specific magnetic fields, at which the nearest-neighbor nuclear spins satisfy a cancellation condition set by their hyperfine and quadrupole couplings. Both the fields and the modulation frequencies follow from an analytical model using computed hyperfine and quadrupole tensors alone, and they shift or vanish upon isotope substitution. At low fields, the field dependence of the coherence time separates the defects into two classes according to the sublattice occupied by carbon. These decoherence fingerprints, directly testable in isotope-engineered samples, establish a structural identification route complementary to optical spectroscopy.
summary: This theoretical study develops a method to structurally identify carbon-based spin qubits in h-BN by analyzing their electron-spin decoherence. By mapping out characteristic spectral modulations (fingerprints) in the coherence time as a function of magnetic field and isotope composition, the authors establish a powerful diagnostic tool complementary to optical methods. This advances the feasibility of using these materials for quantum information processing.
main_problem: The primary challenge is identifying the unknown atomic structures of carbon-based single-spin qubits embedded within hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN).
main_result: The atomic structure of each defect is uniquely imprinted on its electron-spin decoherence fingerprint, providing a structural identification route complementary to optical spectroscopy.
method: The study uses first-principles calculations to map the Hahn-echo and CPMG coherence dynamics of the spin qubits.
model_or_system: The system involves electron spins coupled to a surrounding nuclear spin bath (boron and nitrogen isotopes) within the h-BN lattice. The dynamics are modeled using electron-spin decoherence calculations incorporating hyperfine and quadrupole couplings.
key_observables: Electron-spin-echo envelope modulation (ESEEM) patterns, the magnetic-field dependence of the coherence time ($T_2$), and the specific magnetic fields where modulation occurs.
important_parameters: External magnetic fields (e.g., 500 G, 20000 G), isotopic compositions ($	ext{}^{10}	ext{B}, 	ext{}^{11}	ext{B}, 	ext{}^{14}	ext{N}, 	ext{}^{15}	ext{N}$), and the Transition Boundary (TB) fields.
main_assumptions: The spin density is assumed to be predominantly localized on carbon atoms, leading to coupling mainly via the Fermi contact interaction to nearest-neighbor nuclear spins.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate crystal structures of candidate defects, coherence colormaps showing ESEEM patterns across different isotopes and magnetic fields, and spectra used to pinpoint structural fingerprints.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the spin dynamics by calculating coherence functions for various defects, identifying distinct regimes (low-field vs. high-field) separated by a Transition Boundary, and correlating observed spectral modulations with specific atomic arrangements.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, measurable spectroscopic signature (decoherence fingerprint) derived from fundamental quantum interactions (hyperfine/quadrupole coupling) that can be used to characterize solid-state qubits, which is highly relevant to quantum computing hardware development.
